title: Accelerating Deep Learning Inference in Edge Devices
problem: Deep neural network inference on resource-constrained edge processors requires reducing memory bandwidth, computational overhead, and power consumption while maintaining accuracy. Current approaches struggle to balance the competing demands of inference latency, energy efficiency, and model precision on embedded and mobile devices.
motivation: Deploying efficient DNN inference at the edge enables privacy-preserving, low-latency AI applications without reliance on cloud infrastructure.
method: The approach designs the hardware processor and software model together (called co-design) to run deep neural networks efficiently on resource-limited edge devices. It uses two techniques: quantization, which represents numbers using fewer bits to reduce memory and computation (similar to reducing decimal places), and pruning, which removes weights—the connections in the network—that contribute little to results. By optimizing both the custom hardware accelerator and these compression techniques simultaneously rather than separately, it achieves better efficiency overall.
key_novelty: The core idea is to design the hardware accelerator and compression techniques jointly so they work optimally together, rather than optimizing them in isolation.
contributions: Hardware-software co-design methodology for efficient DNN inference on edge processors
Integration of quantization and pruning techniques tailored to edge hardware constraints
Demonstration of speedup and energy efficiency improvements on edge devices
Practical strategies for maintaining model accuracy under aggressive compression
limitations: The abstract does not discuss limitations or constraints of the approach.
primary_theme: Co-designed quantization and pruning for edge DNN inference
